# Sūciloma Sutta (Snp 2.5 (PTS Snp 47))

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sūciloma Sutta* is the fifth discourse of the Cūḷavagga ("Small Chapter") in the *Suttanipāta* (Snp 2.5, PTS p. 47) [Anderson and Smith 1913; Norman 1997-2001]. Set at the stone couch (*taṅkitamañca*) in Gayā, the text comprises an introductory prose narrative followed by four verses (vv. 270–273) [Anderson and Smith 1913; Dhammika, Middle Land, Middle Way; Levitt 2009]. The yakkha Sūciloma ("Spiky" or "Needle-haired"), in the company of another yakkha named Khara, seeks to test whether the Buddha is a genuine ascetic [DeCaroli 2004; Saddhatissa 2013]. Sūciloma presses his body against the Buddha, who draws back, remarking that the yakkha's touch is disagreeable [DeCaroli 1999; Levitt 2009; Saddhatissa 2013]. Sūciloma threatens to disrupt the Buddha's mind, split his heart, or throw him across the River Ganges if he fails to answer his questions [Bailey, The Raven And The Serpent; Norman 1997-2001; SuttaCentral]. In response to Sūciloma's inquiry regarding the origins of passion (*rāga*), hatred (*dosa*), delight, aversion, and errant thoughts, the Buddha explains that these defilements arise from within oneself (*ito*, glossed by the commentary as *attabhāvato*), like shoots growing from the trunk of a banyan tree [Hamilton 1996; Norman 1997-2001].
The sutta possesses an exact canonical duplicate in the *Yakkha Saṁyutta* (SN 10.3) [Bhikkhu Bodhi 2003; SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse computation in DharmaNexus corroborates extensive Pali-internal overlap with SN 10 (§1.2–8.4 sharing 4,788 characters with SN 10.3 with 0.95 similarity), as well as stock prose shared with the *Āḷavaka Sutta* (Snp 1.10) and verses quoted in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. Verses from the sutta are also cited in several sections of the *Niddesa* (Mnd 1, 14, 16; Cnd 23) [SuttaCentral]. Curated parallels in Chinese Āgama literature include *Saṃyuktāgama* translations (T 99 no. 1324 and T 100 nos. 313, 323; resembling T 99 no. 1314), matching automatic alignments identified by DharmaNexus in T 99 and T 100 [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. In Sanskrit, verse equivalents are preserved in the canonical *Śarīrārthagāthā* embedded in the *Yogācārabhūmi* [Martin 2006; SuttaCentral].
